    Caveats

    9 reasons this chart will not reconcile row-for-row against the printed schedule

    Every one of these ships with the data rather than in a footnote, so a reader who downloads fy2027-adopted.json gets them too. The full text of each is on the caveats page, beside every other document's.

    • No link pairs a transfer's two legs; transfers out exceed transfers in by $50,762,251, the transfers to the Capital Improvement Program.
    • Internal Service charges are billed between city departments, so they are outside the external headline.
    • The city's own book prints two different figures for Internal Service Funds expenditure, $250,000 apart; this chart draws the one on pp.66-67.
    • Beginning and ending working capital are stocks, not flows, so the chart carries no link for them.
    • Permanent Funds are a seventh fund type, and this schedule prints no column for them.
    • A fund's constraint tier is our reading of the Description of Funds narrative, not a figure the city printed.
    • Budget Book pp.127-140 are published twice on this site: the chart draws their adopted columns one year at a time, and the Revenue tables print all four.
    • Every cell of the citywide chart opens into the finer schedules that print it, and they sum back to it to the cent.
    • 4 fund groups' money pp.66-67 print that no fund's own page carries, drawn on a node of the group's own.
